data.name: Maheswar
data.gender_notes: Maheswar is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Mahesh (Mahésh) refers to Lord Shiva in Hindu mythology, the god of destruction and regeneration. Maheswar is a compound of Maha (great) and Ishwara (Lord), meaning 'Lord of the Gods'. The name Maheswar carries the meaning “Lord of the Gods” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Maheswar usually hope their child will grow to embody lord of the gods and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Maheswar belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lord of the Gods.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Maheswar total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

data.cultural_impact: Maheswar is a significant name in Hindu culture, representing the reverence and devotion towards Lord Shiva. In Hindu tradition, Shiva is known as the destroyer of evil, the creator and sustainer of the universe, and the embodiment of detachment and meditation. Celebrating the name Maheswar showcases a deep connection with the Hindu faith and the belief in the power of Lord Shiva.
data.spiritual_significance: Maheswar contains spiritual importance as it is a reminder of the divine presence and power of Lord Shiva. By abiding by this name, individuals give importance and significance to the spiritual aspects of their lives and acknowledge the divine power of Lord Shiva that dwells within and surrounds them. The name Maheswar can serve as a constant reminder to keep one's spiritual center focused on Lord Shiva and the ultimate quest for enlightenment.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Maheshwara signifies the supreme lord, the embodiment of Shiva, the destroyer and transformer in the cycle of life. It represents the divine power to annihilate and recreate, symbolizing the eternal rhythm of creation and destruction.

historical_references.reference: Maheshwara is an ancient Hindu name for Shiva, the god of destruction. This name can be traced back to the Vedic literature, specifically the Rigveda (circa 1500-1000 BCE). In the Rigveda, Rudra, an early form of Shiva, is referred to as Mahadeva, or 'great god'. Over time, this title evolved into Mahadeva Mahadev (great god of gods) and eventually became Maheshwara, or 'lord of Mahadev'.

Maheshwara is also mentioned in the Puranas, a set of Hindu religious texts written between the 4th and 8th centuries CE. In these texts, Shiva is often referred to as Maheshwara, or the 'lord of the universe'. He is depicted as the supreme god, responsible for the creation, preservation, and destruction of the universe.

On YouTube, there are numerous videos on Hindu mythology, prayers, and spiritual practices, where the name Maheswar is mentioned. The name Maheswar is also used in various hashtags and memes related to Hinduism and spirituality.
